en: The Philippine eagle has a wingspan of up to two meters, whereas the national animal, the carabao, can weigh over 1,000 kilograms.
The Philippines officially has 7,641 islands, which is 534 more than the previously taught number of 7,107 islands.
The Philippines celebrated its 125th year of independence in 2023, having declared freedom from Spain on June 12, 1898.
The Philippine government has three co-equal branches, with the Supreme Court comprising exactly 15 justices, including one Chief Justice.
The Philippines has over 180 distinct languages, but only Filipino and English are designated as the two official national languages.
The Giant Lantern Festival in San Fernando features massive, 15-foot-tall rotating wheels illuminated by over 5,000 individual light bulbs.
The National Commission on Indigenous Peoples officially recognizes 110 distinct indigenous groups living across the Philippine archipelago.
Jose Rizal passed the bar exam at age 22 and was proficient in at least 22 different languages.
Governor-General Frank Murphy proclaimed the Sampaguita as the national flower in 1934 after it received the most votes in a public survey.
Fe del Mundo became the first Asian admitted to Harvard Medical School in 1936 and invented a bamboo incubator.
The Philippine flag's sun has exactly eight rays, representing the first eight provinces that revolted against Spanish colonial rule in 1896.
Filipino citizens must be at least 18 years old on election day to vote, a right lowered from 21 years old in 1973.
